verses.1: Jehovam, son of Ahaz, ruled over Israel in Shomron during the twelfth year of Jehosaphat’s reign as king of Judah. He ruled for twenty-two years.
verses.2: He did evil in the eyes of the LORD, but not like his father and mother. He also broke the laws that his father had established.
verses.3: Only in times of great trouble did Jerubbaal, the king who deceived Israel, cease to be a threat to them.
verses.4: And from Sheba, king of the Moabites, he received back for King Israel one hundred thousand sheep and one hundred thousand camels.
verses.5: And it happened that Ahaz sinned against King Hezekiah of Israel.
verses.6: And on that day, King Jehoshaphat left Jerusalem and went out to attack all of Israel.
verses.7: And he went and sent a message to Jehosaphat, the king of Judah. He said, “King Moab is wicked. Let me go to Moab for battle.” But Jehosaphat replied, “I will go with you. We shall be like one nation, just as you are. We shall fight together.”
verses.8: And he said, “This is the path that leads upward.” And he also said, “It’s a path from the desert of Edom.”
verses.9: And the kings of Israel, Judah, and Edom went forth. They traveled for seven days, without any water to drink or food for their animals.
verses.10: And the king of Israel said, “Ah! For Jehovah has called these three kings to give them into Moab’s hands.”
verses.11: And Josaphat said, “Is there no prophet for Jehovah? Let us seek Jehovah from His presence.” Then one of the servants of the king of Israel said, “Elisha, son of Shaphta, who can cross the river with his hands raised?”
verses.12: And Josaphat said, “There is a message from the LORD.” Then the king of Israel and Josaphat came to him.
verses.13: And Elisha said to the king of Israel, “What is your purpose in going to the prophets of your father and those of your mother? The king replied, “When Jehovah calls these three kings to give them into Moab’s hands.”
verses.14: And Elisha said, “May the Lord’s army stand before me. I have no fear of Jehovah the king of Judah. I will speak to you, and if you accept my words, then I will be safe.”
verses.15: And now, give me a musician. Let him be the musician who will play music. And let the hand of Jehovah be upon him.
verses.16: And he said, “As Jehovah said, this river has been made to flow in a winding path.”
verses.17: “For thus said the LORD: ‘Do not see any wind or any rain. This river will fill with water, and you will drink from it, along with your animals.’”
verses.18: And it was pleasing to the eyes of Jehovah, and He handed over Moab into your hands.
verses.19: And every city that was destroyed by war, and every city that was conquered by enemies, all the good trees will be cut down. All the watersheds will be dried up. And all the good parts of the land will be covered with stones.
verses.20: And in the morning, as the blood was poured out, water came from Adam’s direction. The earth was filled with water.
verses.21: And all those who heard this, thought that the kings were going to fight against them. They cried out in despair from every corner and every place. They stood on the borders.
verses.22: In the morning, they stood up. The sun shone over the waters. They saw that the waters were red, like blood.
verses.23: And they said, “This blood is the sign of their destruction. The kings have been destroyed, and one man has killed his neighbor. Now let us go to battle.”
verses.24: And they came to the camp of Israel. Israel stood up, and they attacked Moab. They fought against them, and they defeated Moab.
verses.25: And the cities will be destroyed, and every good thing will be thrown away. All springs of water will dry up, and every good tree will be cut down, with its roots left behind in the ground. The branches will be cut off, and everything will be destroyed.
verses.26: And King Moab saw that he was stronger than him in battle. So he took seven thousand men, who were skilled in warfare, to go to King Adam and not be defeated by him.
verses.27: And he took his son, the king who would rule under him, and carried him onto the burning fire. There was a great explosion caused by that fire, and the Israelites fled from there. They returned to their own land.
